newsitem.title: UK: Shield says AFT test "significant" tool.
newsitem.headline: Shield says AFT test "significant" tool.

text.p: Britain's Shield Diagnostics Plc said on Monday clinical trials of its diagnostic test for Activated Factor Twelve (AFT) pointed towards AFT becoming a "significant" tool to assess cardiovascular risk in the population as a whole.

Shield said in a statement that data from the tests showed higher levels of AFT were associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease and that the percentage difference in AFT between individuals at low risk compared to those at high risk was greater than observed with other markers.

"We at Shield have always believed AFT would be a significant product...I have every confidence in the ability of the Shield team to commercialise the product and create significant shareholder value," Shield chairman Hamish Hale said in a statement.

Shield said AFT levels increased with increasing risk of cardiovascular disease. It said two separate studies showed there was more than a 30 percent higher level of AFT in patients with coronary artery disease compared to healthy controls.
This compared to around seven percent for cholesterol and 14 percent for fibrinogen in the same patients. Day to day variation of AFT in individuals was much less than cholesterol, Shield said.
Shield said AFT levels were also found to be consistent over time in individuals which improved the ability to classify accurately patients with one test result.
It said other markers such as cholesterol and fibrinogen used to predict risk on single test results could give rise to misclassification due to their high variability within individuals.
